offence_severity: Rigorous Imprisonment for Life and INR 50,000 Fine (1 year RI in default)
premeditation_planning: Court found premeditation/planning as part of conspiracy
key_evidence_accepted: The Supreme Court accepted that there is sufficient material on record giving rise to reasonable doubt as to the involvement of the appellants in the crime, and that the appellants were not present at the spot where the crime was committed nor any direct/speciﬁc role in commission of the oﬀence being attributed to them.
witness_credibility: The court assessed the main witnesses (PW1, PW2 and PW7) as having testimonies that were successfully challenged by the appellants, leading to reasonable doubt about their credibility and the overall prosecution narrative.
post_offence_conduct: The assailant/shooter, who is absconding, is noted in the judgment, but no specific conduct of the accused after the offence is stated.
trial_duration: Dates of offence: 12.05.1995; Trial judgment: 27.11.2002; High Court decision: 05.11.2009; Supreme Court decision: 26.07.2023
legal_representation: Vinay Navre, P. R. Rajhans, Amarnath Gupta, Jayant Kumar, Janmejay Verma, Ms. Hardikaa, Vishal Arun, Dr. Sushil Balwada, Kaushal Yadav, Nandlal Kumar Mishra, Srilok Nath Rath, Ms. Reena Rao, Kashyap Kumar Dwivedi, Advs. for the Appellant; Rahul Chitnis, Siddharth Dharmadhikari, Aaditya Aniruddha Pande, Bharat Bagla, Sourav Singh, Aditya Krishna, Advs. for the Respondent
investigation_status: First Information Report lodged on 13.05.1995; Investigation culminated into a chargesheet against 10 persons; 3 were discharged and 7 stood trial
appeal_history: Trial court: Convictions of A4 and A2; High Court: Dismissed appeals and upheld convictions; Supreme Court: Appeals allowed
prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that the appellants (A4 and A2) were part of a criminal conspiracy to abduct and murder the deceased, with A1 and A7 as the masterminds. They claimed that the appellants were present at the crime scene and played a direct role in the commission of the offense.
defence_argument: The defence argued that there was reasonable doubt regarding the involvement of the appellants in the crime. They pointed out inconsistencies in the prosecution's witnesses' testimonies, the absence of direct evidence linking the appellants to the crime, and the acquittal of the main conspirators A1 and A7.
legal_principle_applied: The Supreme Court applied the principle that a conviction cannot be sustained in the presence of reasonable doubt, emphasizing the presumption of innocence and the necessity for the prosecution to prove its case beyond reasonable doubt.
precedent_relied_upon: Noor Mohammad Mohd. Yusuf Momin v. State of Maharashtra AIR 1971 SC 885; State of Uttar Pradesh v. Krishna Gopal (1988) 4 SCC 302; State of Madhya Pradesh v. Dharkole (2004) 13 SCC 308; Coﬃn v. United States, 156 US 432 (1895); Narendra Singh v. State of Madhya Pradesh (2004) 10 SCC 699; Ranjeetsing Brahmajeetsing Sharma v. State of Maharashtra (2005) 5 SCC 294
